title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
The couple encountered a fraud deployment in which criminals built an AI-generated fake website designed to display false investment account information. The deceptive interface created the impression of legitimate trading activity and modest returns, which built enough trust for the victims to deposit larger sums. The fraudsters used a known tactic: allowing small withdrawals to succeed before trapping funds in larger ones.

The system failure was one of trust without verification. The victims had no independent way to confirm that the trading platform showed real positions and real money, only what the interface displayed to them. They were using a legitimate trading app, but criminals had overlaid a false version that hid the actual destination of their funds. A human verification step, such as requiring confirmation through a separate communication channel or independent account audit before large withdrawals, could have caught the discrepancy before the loss reached $800,000.

It is not established whether the trading app itself was compromised, whether the fake website exploited a vulnerability in the app, or whether victims were directed to a counterfeit app entirely. The role of the initial WhatsApp contact and how the scammers gained credibility remains part of the scheme but is not detailed in the reporting.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired couple in Georgia lost nearly $800,000 in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. Jerry and Mindy Dunaway were convinced to invest money through a mobile trading app, and initially saw modest returns and were able to withdraw funds, which built their confidence. The scammers used an AI-generated fake website that displayed false information about the couple's investments on their screens while taking their money.

The couple discovered the fraud when Jerry tried to make a larger withdrawal and couldn't access the funds. Police confirmed that while the trading app was legitimate, criminals had created a deceptive overlay to trick investors. Though the Dunaways are working with local police, investigators say victims in these cases rarely recover their money. Their children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help the couple with daily expenses as they attempt to rebuild their lives.
